original.target_description: Reuter (2011), section 3: web-search comparison of feel/have pain expressions across low/high intensity attributes, three search engines, and first-person/gerund phrase forms. This is the named primary study, but the supplied study-1 locator does not identify a particular inferential test among these descriptive comparisons, and no Kendall’s W test is reported.

n.sample_role: Search hits/webpages are counted; no explicit critical-test analytic sample size is stated. Attribute, phrase-form and search-engine counts are distinct descriptive roles, not a documented analytic N.
n.exclusions: Appendix describes omitted duplicate hits with possible residual duplicates; strong/great/huge and other listed attributes were excluded, retaining four low-intensity and four high-intensity attributes. Hits across phrases/engines are not documented as mutually exclusive final groups.
n.location: Manuscript pp. 13–16, Appendix: Methods and Search Statistics; Tables 3–5

notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text names Kevin Reuter, Distinguishing the Appearance from the Reality of Pain, and Journal of Consciousness Studies, 18, No. 9–10, 2011. It includes the full argument, empirical section, conclusion, references, and methods/search-statistics appendix (16 manuscript pages). This supports primary author-manuscript identity against the neutral reference, rather than a secondary excerpt or preregistration. Pagination is manuscript-local (the journal page range is printed as ??–??); no DOI is printed, so the input identifier art00005 is not independently confirmed as a DOI. No source PDF was supplied. Inspected the complete supplied text. The empirical results are descriptive ratios in Table 1, corpus percentages in Table 2, and search-hit counts/ratios in Tables 3–5. Kendall’s W, another formal effect coefficient/test statistic, and numerical p values/bounds are not reported. No effect-size conversion or statistical reconstruction was performed. Search counts differ across engines/phrase forms, and the text says engines search the same forums/articles/blogs, precluding a justified disjoint-hit sum. No N was derived from the number of attributes, cells, hits or degrees of freedom. Exact critical-test correspondence remains unresolved; target_match is null, despite confirmed paper identity. Replication and reported-success records are unassigned placeholders.
